problem: Existing active view acquisition methods (e.g. FisherRF, Ray Entropy) pick next-best-views by maximizing information gain over the whole scene, wasting limited views on regions irrelevant to robot safety and ignoring collision risk.
motivation: A payload robot follows a predefined path using a 3D Gaussian Splatting map built from few views, so map uncertainty can bias collision-risk assessment. An auxiliary camera robot has limited time and energy, so its views should be spent on safety-critical regions near the path.
key_idea: Compute a coherent risk measure (AVaR) of collision from the uncertain 3D Gaussian map at each waypoint, use it to set a risk-dependent masking radius, and run FisherRF-style expected-information-gain NBV selection only on the masked safety-critical Gaussians.
insight: Restricting the information-gain computation to risk-masked Gaussians reduces the Wasserstein-2 distance to the ground-truth closest-distance distribution for both FisherRF and Ray Entropy, so the gain is algorithm-agnostic. The ablation shows that a dynamic, AVaR-based radius (0.370) beats every uniform radius (best 0.392 at 0.5). Expected-value-based masking is said to underestimate risk near obstacles (qualitative figure only).
method: 3DGS map with uncertainty: SplaTAM-style isotropic 3D Gaussians x_i~N(mu_i, sigma_i^2 I) trained on RGB-D with L1 color+depth loss
Signed distance statistics: the distance from waypoint p to a Gaussian is normal, N(||mu_i-p||, sigma_i^2) (anisotropic case in appendix)
AVaR collision risk: closed form AVaR_eps = ||mu_i-p|| - sigma_i/(sqrt(2pi) eps exp(iota^2)); the waypoint risk alpha_k is the min over all Gaussians
Risk-aware Environment Masking: radius r_mask(k)=beta1*exp(-beta2*alpha_k); keep only Gaussians inside the union of balls around the waypoints

NBV with RaEM: choose the candidate pose maximizing the Fisher-information EIG (trace of the candidate Hessian times the inverse train Hessian, diagonal Laplace approximation) computed over the masked Gaussians only
Alternative level-set risk: an A_eps measure with a cutoff distance d_s (appendix, not evaluated)

setting.backbone: SplaTAM-style 3D Gaussian Splatting with FisherRF (and Ray Entropy with an implicit occupancy network) for NBV selection; no policy network
setting.training_data: Per-scene online optimization only (60 iterations per acquired view, 660 total), no pretraining or extra data
setting.observation: RGB-D 256x256 from an aerial camera robot
setting.action_space: Candidate camera poses (250 random per stage), reached via the Habitat pathfinder shortest action sequence
setting.privileged: none for NBV; ground-truth point clouds from Matterport3D are used only for evaluation

results: On 10 Matterport3D scenes, RaEM lowers the W2 distance to the ground-truth risk distribution by 24.26% with FisherRF and 17.63% with Ray Entropy. It also beats uniform-radius masking (0.370 vs best 0.392).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation, on a few scenes with a fixed 10-waypoint path and a single set of masking hyperparameters; no real robot and no actual navigation success or collision rate
Assumes a predefined path and static scenes; the risk model treats Gaussians as independent, and only the worst-case Gaussian counts
The paper is short and lacks a task-level navigation evaluation; the comparison with expected-value masking is qualitative only
